title: Burst metrics cardinality review (Dedicated Burst pools)
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture decisions on metric names + allowed dimensions for the Dedicated “burst capacity” feature.
- Avoid high-cardinality blowups in Prometheus/Mimir while still enabling:
  (a) SRE pool health + saturation diagnosis
  (b) routing/admission debugging
  (c) customer transparency views (likely via a separate analytics path)

Context
- Burst adds new signals: admission allow/deny, pool saturation, per-tenant burst usage attribution.
- Naively labeling everything by tenant_id + model + region + pool would create unbounded series.
- Existing constraints:
  - We’re using Prometheus-compatible metrics with remote write into Mimir (cost scales with active series).
  - Dashboards for oncall need low-latency, high-reliability time series.
  - Detailed per-tenant usage is already handled better in usage/metering pipelines (ClickHouse / lake + aggregation jobs) and logs/traces.

Working session
- Date: 2025-06-24 (30m)
- Attendees: Allison (obs), Logan (telemetry), Nadia (metering), Caleb (ingestion), Sergio (dashboards), Peter (routing SRE embed)

Principles (agreed)
1) No tenant_id in always-on Prometheus counters/histograms.
   - Exception only for a tightly controlled allowlist (pilot tenants), and even then prefer “exemplars + traces” over labels.
2) Keep pool identifiers bounded.
   - pool_id is OK if the set of pools is small and managed (e.g., per region + gpu_type + pool_class). Avoid per-cluster unique IDs if they churn.
3) Avoid raw model name labels in hot-path metrics.
   - Prefer model_family/model_class (e.g., “llama3”, “qwen2”, “mixtral”) or model_size_bucket (7b/13b/70b) where feasible.
   - For routing-level debugging of a specific model version, rely on logs/traces and targeted “debug metrics” behind a flag.
4) Region is OK; AZ is not.
   - Region is bounded and required operationally. AZ tends to multiply series and isn’t needed for burst v1.
5) Favor gauges for pool health + counters for admission, with minimal label sets.
6) For customer transparency, use the metering pipeline with explicit dimensionality (tenant_id is expected there) rather than Prometheus.

Decisions: allowed label dimensions
Allowed (safe / bounded)
- region (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1)
- pool_class (baseline_dedicated, burst_shared) — burst metrics mostly pool_class=burst_shared
- gpu_type (A100-80G, H100-80G; keep list small, align to fleet taxonomy)
- pool_name OR pool_key (bounded string; see below)
- decision (admit | deny)
- deny_reason (bounded enum; see deny reason list)
- tenant_tier (pilot | beta | ga) OR plan_tier (Dedicated-Standard, Dedicated-Enterprise) if we need segmentation
- route_fallback (none | fallback_baseline | fallback_burst | fallback_other_region | deny) — bounded enum

Not allowed (default)
- tenant_id / account_id / org_id
- model (full name) or model_version
- request_id, trace_id
- endpoint_id / deployment_id if it’s customer-defined and unbounded
- hostname/pod
- AZ

“Pool identity” guidance
- We need something to disambiguate pools for oncall without exploding series.
- Proposal: pool_key := {region}:{gpu_type}:{pool_class}:{pool_generation}
  - Example: us-east-1:H100-80G:burst_shared:g1
  - pool_generation increments only when we intentionally roll pool topology, not per autoscaling event.
- Avoid embedding cluster_id / nodepool_id.
- Fleet team should guarantee pool_key cardinality stays < ~50 globally for v1.

Deny reason taxonomy (bounded enum)
- not_enabled (tenant not enabled for burst)
- policy_limit_concurrency (tenant concurrency cap)
- policy_limit_tps (tenant tokens/sec cap)
- cooldown_active (tenant cooldown/backoff active)
- pool_saturated (burst pool at/over saturation gate)
- region_not_eligible (no burst pool in region / gpu mismatch)
- authz_failed (policy claims / signature invalid)
- internal_error (policy/routing failure; should page if elevated)

Metric set (proposed) + dimensions

A) Admission metrics (routing / policy)
1) burst_admission_requests_total
- Type: counter
- Emitted: routing layer (post-policy decision, before dispatch)
- Labels (allowed): region, pool_key, decision, deny_reason (only when decision=deny), tenant_tier, route_fallback
- Notes:
  - No tenant_id.
  - deny_reason must be from enum above; default to internal_error only when truly unknown.

2) burst_admission_latency_ms
- Type: histogram
- Labels (allowed): region, tenant_tier
- Notes:
  - Do NOT slice histograms by pool_key and deny_reason simultaneously; too many series.
  - If we need pool-level latency, add a separate gauge based on sampled spans.

B) Pool health metrics (fleet)
3) burst_pool_allocatable_gpus
- Type: gauge
- Labels: region, pool_key, gpu_type

4) burst_pool_in_use_gpus
- Type: gauge
- Labels: region, pool_key, gpu_type

5) burst_pool_saturation_ratio
- Type: gauge (in_use/allocatable after smoothing)
- Labels: region, pool_key, gpu_type
- Notes:
  - This is what dashboards and alerts should primarily use.

6) burst_pool_queue_depth
- Type: gauge (if applicable)
- Labels: region, pool_key
- Notes:
  - Only if we have a meaningful queue concept; otherwise skip to avoid false confidence.

C) Usage attribution (shadow metering + coarse operational view)
7) burst_tokens_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: region, pool_key, usage_class (baseline | burst)
- Notes:
  - This is operational, not billing-grade. Billing-grade attribution is via the metering pipeline.

8) burst_requests_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: region, pool_key, usage_class

D) Neighbor protection (SRE-facing)
9) dedicated_neighbor_p99_latency_ms
- Type: gauge (computed from service-level histograms) OR histogram summary panel
- Labels: region, gpu_type, pool_class
- Notes:
  - We should avoid “tenant slice” here. This is to catch broad regressions.

10) dedicated_tail_latency_regression_events_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: region, pool_class, severity (info | warn | crit)
- Notes:
  - Optional; if we keep it, ensure severity is bounded.

Pilot-only / debug-only (behind a feature flag + allowlist)
- burst_admission_requests_total_by_tenant (TEMP)
  - Labels: tenant_id, region, decision, deny_reason
  - Guardrails:
    - Allowlist max 3 tenants (design partners)
    - Auto-disable if active series > threshold
    - Time-boxed: remove before GA
  - Alternative preferred: logs + traces with structured fields.

Logs/traces: where tenant_id/model/version should live
- Decision: per-request debugging should rely on:
  - Structured logs fields:
    - tenant_id, deployment_id, request_model, resolved_model, region, pool_key, admission_decision, deny_reason, cooldown_state, circuit_breaker_state
  - Traces:
    - routing span tagged similarly; use exemplars to link from time series anomalies to traces
- Reason: high-cardinality fields are appropriate in logs/traces with sampling + retention controls.

Alerting implications (Sergio/Peter)
- Alerts should be based on bounded dimensions:
  - pool saturation high (burst_pool_saturation_ratio > 0.9 for 10m) by pool_key
  - admission deny rate high (burst_admission_requests_total{decision="deny"} / total > X) by region/pool_key, but do not slice by deny_reason in the paging condition (use deny_reason only in dashboard drill-down)
  - internal_error deny_reason elevated should page (since indicates bug, not capacity)
- Any alert that would page “by tenant_id” is not allowed.

Open questions
1) Model dimension: do we need model_family on admission metrics?
- Pro: helps identify a single large model driving saturation.
- Con: risk of creep + model families proliferate.
- Tentative: include model_family only if we cap to a controlled enum (Telemetry team to maintain list). Otherwise stick to pool-level view.

2) Pool_key churn: will pool_generation churn during incidents/autoscaling?
- Action: Fleet (Samantha/Vanessa) to confirm pool_key stability and expected max cardinality.

3) Customer transparency: how do we build per-tenant dashboards without Prometheus labels?
- Proposed approach:
  - Console uses metering tables (tenant_id, timestamp, usage_class, tokens, requests, rejects by reason) with hourly aggregation
  - For near-real-time, use a separate low-cardinality aggregation service keyed by tenant_id with controlled fanout (not raw Prometheus)
- Action: Nadia + Chloe to confirm feasibility for beta.

Action items
- [Logan] Update ENG-4826 implementation plan with label restrictions + deny_reason enum (2025-06-28)
- [Caleb] Add series budget guardrails / monitors for new burst metrics in ingestion (2025-07-02)
- [Sergio] Ensure dashboards in PR-391 do not assume tenant_id metrics exist; add drill-down links to logs/traces (2025-07-03)
- [Nadia] Document the intended “billing vs operational metrics” split for burst (shadow metering vs Prometheus) (2025-07-05)
- [Allison] Post summary in #eng-sre and #eng-platform with “Not allowed” label list + rationale (2025-06-25)

Notes to self / reminders
- Be strict early: label creep happens during incident pressure (someone asks for tenant_id labels “temporarily”). Pre-plan debug workflows via logs/traces so oncall has a path.
- If pilot insists on per-tenant real-time graphs, push it into a controlled aggregation endpoint rather than Prometheus.
- Watch out for “deployment_id” (customer-supplied) sneaking into labels via routing metrics.
